title: Try to be a kid again and just have fun making games
author: Orlandogameschool
selftext:
As my user name implies I used to teach game development. Unity, scratch, UDK, Roblox studio ect. 

I taught k-12 

When I was teaching  I was the struggling game dev. I never shipped anything never released any game ideas. 

I showed one-class a simple unity game I made. You fly around as an angel, ugly low poly game. 

Really really simple prototype  
   
One of my students came back over the weekend and was like what’s going on. I tried to download your game when I got home and I couldn’t find it……that moment right there changed my whole outlook on making games. Are you doing this to make money? Or make fun games that people like to play?

Ai is helping me revive projects from over 10 years ago.its helping me understand code on a much deeper level. Stop worrying about the haters and just make fun games.

comments.author: kal101246
comments.body: Honestly yeah these tools are allowing me to be a game dev for the first time in 10 years because it's breaking down the barrier for coding. I stopped back in the day because it was too tedious and I didn't have the time or passion to commit to learning how to become a better game programmer. Now I can focus on all the other parts of game development and just try my best to make whatever i think is fun or interesting!

replies.author: kazuyette
replies.body:
I'm not alone ! I feel exactly the same. I always wanted to be able to code games. I never had the ressource, time, money ... to learn efficiently on my own. 

And now thanks to AI , I can be the "producer"of my game like Hideo Kojima ( 😃) , throw tons of ideas at Claude and let it do all the coding phase 😄

replies.author: Orlandogameschool
replies.body:
Ok I’m happy to read this! You just made my day haha I was never really good at coding I’m a artist at heart I love graphic design I love 3d modeling ai allows me to be creative with the game design and code without spending weeks digging though Reddit and substack trying to understand why unity keeps crashing or whatever. 

I took about 5 years off started teaching tha got me back in but like you I just didn’t have the time to learn c# then boom ai comes and I haven’t touched my ps5 in weeks just making all these silly game ideas  I’ve had over the years

comments.author: SonderSoft
comments.body:
You see the big picture. That's beautiful. Chase the dream and share it with others.


Anger and resentment is rife following years of defunding the arts and a cost-of-living crisis, and it's no wonder why so many have identified generative AI as their coup-de-grace crusade.


Hammers can kill just as well as they can build. Weild your hammer and help the eagles fly once more.

comments.author: kazuyette
comments.body: I'm on the same page buddy. I'm making my little AI game to share it with the world and that someone, somewhere on Earth is enjoying playing my game as much as I enjoy making it.

comments.author: NovelFlame_AI
comments.body:
Indeed when you're a kid making games, you don't sit there wondering if your project is disrupting an industry or optimizing a funnel. 😅 You make a game because it'd be cool if somebody got to play it.

One of the nice things about AI  in my view is that it's lowered the cost of following random creative impulses. Some of them turn out terrible. Some turn out surprisingly fun. Both are probably healthier than spending six months talking yourself out of starting!

replies.author: Orlandogameschool
replies.body: Dude you said it better than I could! “Lowering the cost of random creative  impulses is exactly what ai has done for me. I’ve always been an idea guy ai allows me to visualize the idea much much sooner. Ai would have saved me a lot of time in my 20s I’ll just say that 😂

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: I mean, anyone who goes into game dev simply to make money is choosing the wrong fucking industry for their 'Get Rich Quick' mentality. You can certainly make money with game dev, which is nice, but there's no way someone is going to have the drive and commitment required to get to that point unless they're making games for other reasons. Frankly, I still maintain that unless the game in your head is one you want to play more than anything else, and that you'll play the shit out of (in concept) then it's not going to be successful. Because if you're not part of the intended audience for the game, how the hell are you going to gauge what features it should have and how it should feel? I think this is highlighted by people who drop into this sub looking for ideas on games to make.  If you're not making a game that every fiber of your being is pointing you towards, I just don't know how you'd be able to stick with it after the 3rd rebuild and 189 hours dumped into a feature that you can't get feeling right (in reality you probably wouldn't even be able to tell that the feature doesn't feel right, in that case, so I guess you'd be relying on testers to give you nebulous critique on it instead.)
